description: Count inclusion-wise minimal dominating sets in a permutation graph using the five-tuple DAG.

source.title: On the Enumeration and Counting of Minimal Dominating sets in Interval and Permutation Graphs
source.publisher: Proceedings of ISAAC 2013, Lecture Notes in Computer Science 8283
source.implementation_status: bounded clean-room count profile of the permutation-graph Initial/Regular DAG

input.encoding: [n, pi_0, ..., pi_(n-1)]; vertex i is the segment from bottom rank i to top rank pi_i

output.encoding: exact number of inclusion-wise minimal dominating sets

contract.graph_model: Vertices are indexed by their bottom-line order. Distinct vertices i<j are adjacent exactly when pi_i>pi_j; the supplied pi values must be a permutation of 0..n-1.
contract.primary_method: Build the paper's permutation-graph DAG states (i,j,k,r,s), classified as Initial or Regular using the five relative-order cases for the final three selected segments. Derive each admissible successor (j,k,l,r',s') on demand from conditions A.1–A.5 and count paths backward from final states. Count minimal dominating sets of sizes one and two directly as in Theorem 20.
contract.independent_method: Enumerate every nonempty vertex subset, test domination by union of closed-neighborhood bitmasks, and require each selected vertex to have a closed-neighborhood private witness not covered by the other selected vertices.
contract.invalid_cases: Null or empty input, n outside 1..8, wrong length, trailing values, negative/out-of-range ranks, duplicate ranks, or signed extreme ranks return -1.
contract.count_bound: Every output counts a subset of the nonempty subsets of at most eight vertices, hence is at most 255 and fits signed i64.

complexity.primary_time: O(n^8), matching the source DAG construction and path-counting bound; successors are derived rather than stored.
complexity.primary_space: (n+1)^5 signed-i64 path-count entries; at n=8 this is 59,049 entries or 472,392 bytes, plus bounded graph and local state.
complexity.independent_time: O(2^n*n^2) subset, coverage, and single-vertex-removal checks.
complexity.independent_space: O(n) neighborhood bitmasks and scalar subset state.
